question: What happens when body tissue successfully regenerates?

options.A: The injured area remains permanently open and weak
options.B: A tough fibrous scar replaces the original tissue
options.C: Damaged cells are replaced by identical new cells
options.D: Fat cells multiply to fill the empty space left behind

explanation: Regeneration restores the exact same cell type, returning the tissue to its original structure and function. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h1)

question: Why does the body form a scar instead of regenerating original tissue in some organs?

options.A: Scars require less energy for the body to produce than normal skin
options.B: Fibrous tissue prevents future infections from entering the wound
options.C: The original cells lack the ability to divide and replace themselves
options.D: Scar tissue contracts much faster than healthy muscle tissue

explanation: When specialized cells cannot multiply, the body uses fibrous connective tissue to bridge the gap and maintain structural integrity. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is the main goal of the hemostasis phase when a fresh wound occurs?

options.A: To destroy bacteria using white blood cells
options.B: To stretch the skin edges back together
options.C: To build new collagen fibers across the gap
options.D: To stop bleeding by forming a blood clot

explanation: Hemostasis involves blood vessel constriction and platelet clumping to quickly halt blood loss. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a classic sign of the inflammatory phase?
explanation: Inflammation causes redness, heat, swelling, and pain due to increased blood flow and fluid movement, while permanent numbness is not a normal sign. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which cells are mainly responsible for producing collagen during wound healing?
explanation: Fibroblasts migrate into the wound during proliferation and secrete the collagen needed to rebuild tissue strength. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why does healthy granulation tissue look pink or red and bleed easily?

options.A: It contains a dense network of newly formed, fragile capillaries
options.B: It is packed with old, stagnant blood cells waiting to be cleared
options.C: It lacks any blood supply and relies entirely on surface moisture
options.D: It consists purely of thick, hardened layers of dead white blood cells

explanation: The bright red color comes from angiogenesis, which creates tiny, delicate blood vessels to nourish the healing area. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h3)

question: How does collagen change during the remodeling phase of wound healing?

options.A: It is completely dissolved and replaced with liquid fat cells
options.B: It stops growing entirely after the first week of injury
options.C: It is reorganized into neat, strong lines that increase tissue strength
options.D: It turns into hard bone to protect the underlying muscle

explanation: Random collagen bundles are broken down and re-laid in an organized pattern, greatly improving the tensile strength of the scar. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h4)

question: What type of healing occurs when a clean surgical incision is closed with sutures?
explanation: Primary intention happens when clean wound edges are brought together directly, resulting in minimal scarring. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why does a wound healing by secondary intention take longer to close?

options.A: Blood clots refuse to form in open wounds of this type
options.B: The body must fill a large tissue gap with granulation tissue from the bottom up
options.C: Inflammation is completely absent, slowing down cell division
options.D: Sutures physically block the skin cells from growing across the surface

explanation: Because the edges cannot be brought together, the body needs extra time to produce granulation tissue and contract the wound. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h5)

question: A postpartum mother with a perineal tear has a poor diet lacking protein and vitamin C. How will this affect her healing?

options.A: It will prevent any blood clots from forming during hemostasis
options.B: It will make her skin turn permanently yellow in color
options.C: It will slow down collagen production and weaken the repair
options.D: It will cause her blood pressure to drop dangerously low

explanation: Protein and vitamin C are essential building blocks for fibroblasts to manufacture strong collagen fibers. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h6)

question: How does a localized wound infection delay the normal healing process?

options.A: It traps the wound in a prolonged state of damaging inflammation
options.B: It turns all granulation tissue into hard bone instantly
options.C: It stops fibroblasts from ever entering the body
options.D: It forces the wound to heal too fast, causing the skin to split

explanation: Infection keeps white blood cells fighting bacteria continuously, preventing the wound from moving into the proliferation phase. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T10#BMP111_U1_T10_h6)
